title: A gate stamps per option, so one stamp can hold two runs and one run two stamps
body:
## Summary

`run_gate` stamps each option's artefact pair at the moment **that option starts**, not once per `check`/`test` invocation. So the minute stamp is not a run identifier, and two things follow that nothing in the output says:

- **One run spans two stamps.** A `check all` starting at 18:34:58 wrote `20260901-1834.SYNTAX` and `20260901-1834.LINT`, then `20260901-1835.{CRITIC,FORMAT,TOOLCHAIN}`.
- **One stamp spans two runs.** `20260901-1835` contains `CRITIC/FORMAT/TOOLCHAIN` from the run that **FAILED lint**, and `LINT/SYNTAX` from the next run, which **passed**.

## Why this is worse than untidy

Grouping artefacts by their stamp prefix is the obvious thing to do and it silently mixes runs. Both directions produce a wrong verdict from correct files:

- Pair the failing run's `1835.CRITIC/FORMAT/TOOLCHAIN` with the passing run's `1835.LINT` and a **failed run reads as green**. That is the cardinal sin, assembled entirely out of honest artefacts.
- Pair the other way and a green run reads as failed, which costs an investigation rather than a release.

**Nothing in any file names its run.** The `.out` and `.errors` pair carry the option and the minute, and the minute is exactly the field a reader will use as the run key because it is the only candidate present.

## How it was found (2026-09-01)

Verifying a genuinely-green `check all` before a fleet re-vendor. `ls -t | head -1` on `*LINT.out` returned the previous run's file; the counter in it said `33 file(s), 0 breach(es)`, which was true and belonged to a different run. Resolving it required `stat`-ing mtimes and reconstructing run boundaries by hand.

The verdict itself was correct in this instance -- run 2 really did run all five options with 0-byte seals and `33 file(s)` on both counted gates. **The defect is that establishing that took manual mtime archaeology, and the cheap reading was wrong.**

## Related

Adjacent to `0034` (a seal records the result and not the scope) but distinct: `0034` is about the reach of one seal, this is about which seals belong to the same run. A fix for `0034` that does not give a run an identity leaves this open.

## Fix direction (not prescriptive)

Stamp once per invocation and pass that stamp to every option, so an artefact set is addressable by construction. A monotonic run id, or the existing `-SS` suffix form applied uniformly, would both do it. **Whatever is chosen, the acceptance test is that a reader can enumerate exactly one run's artefacts without consulting mtimes.**
